stories.head: Iran vows to use 'all available means' against US naval blockade
stories.say: Iran says it will use every means it has to counter the American naval blockade, a day after Donald Trump threatened to sink Iranian tankers that try to break it.
stories.stand: Tehran called the blockade an act of military aggression after Donald Trump warned that ships trying to break it would be sunk.
body: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baghaei, said on Monday that Iran would use all available means to counter what he called US aggression. He said sanctions and the naval blockade amounted to military aggression and cited Article 51 of the UN Charter.

The statement came a day after President Donald Trump warned that Iranian ships trying to break the blockade would go to the bottom of the sea. The US first imposed the blockade on 13 April, lifted it in June and restored it on 14 July after a draft understanding collapsed.

Baghaei dismissed reports of Iranian ships loading oil as speculation. Iranian officials say there is no concrete plan for a tanker convoy, though media linked to the Revolutionary Guards say plans are being drawn up.

stories.head: Zelenskyy says Ukrainian sea drones sank a Russian corvette off Libya
stories.say: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine used seven sea drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya, sinking the corvette Merkury. Libyan officials describe it as severely damaged.
stories.stand: Ukraine's president claimed the attack in Benghazi on Sunday; Libyan officials said the warship was badly damaged and the UN called for an inquiry.
body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that Ukraine was behind drone attacks on two Russian ships off Libya on Sunday. He said seven Ukrainian-made naval drones were used and that the corvette Merkury was sunk.
He said Ukraine also hit the dry cargo ship MV Angara, which he said Russia used to carry weapons, and destroyed a Ka-27 helicopter. Two Libyan officials told AP the corvette was severely damaged.
Libya's eastern health ministry said all crew of the Angara had been rescued. The UN Support Mission in Libya called for an immediate, independent and transparent investigation.

stories.head: Russian strikes on Kyiv region kill at least 15
stories.say: At least fifteen people have been killed in Russian strikes on the Kyiv region. Eleven died when a block of flats partly collapsed in Dymer, and three at a supermarket in Vyshneve.
stories.stand: Most of the dead were in a partly collapsed block of flats in Dymer, where rescuers were still searching on Monday.
body: Russian drone and missile attacks on the Kyiv region have killed at least 15 people, Al Jazeera reported on Monday, citing Ukrainian officials.

In Dymer, about 45km north of Kyiv, a strike on a five-storey building killed at least 11 people, said regional official Tymur Tkachenko. The State Emergency Service said rescuers were still searching for 11 people, including two children.
In Vyshneve, south of Kyiv, a strike on a supermarket killed three people and wounded 15, Mayor Illya Dikov said. One person was killed in a strike on a house in Bila Tserkva.

stories.head: At least 24 killed in Indonesian sweet factory fire, police say
stories.say: At least twenty-four people have died in a fire at a sweet factory in Indonesia's Banten province, police say. The bodies will need DNA tests to be identified.
stories.stand: The blaze broke out on Saturday at a three-storey factory in Serang regency, west of Jakarta, and dozens of workers were still unaccounted for.
body: A fire at a sweet factory in Serang regency, Banten province, has killed at least 24 people, Indonesian police said. The blaze began on Saturday afternoon and was put out the next morning.

The factory belongs to PT Fonusa Agung Mulia, which makes the Milkita milk sweet brand. Authorities said late on Sunday that 63 people were believed to have been in the affected area, with 34 still missing.

Police said the bodies could not be identified visually and DNA testing would be needed. A presidential adviser said the fire may have started with a short circuit in an air-conditioning system, but stressed that investigations continue.

stories.head: Mexico arrests eight more after capture of cartel boss 'Chapo Isidro'
stories.say: Mexican troops have arrested eight more suspects linked to Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, the cartel boss on the FBI's most wanted list who was captured in Sinaloa on Friday.
stories.stand: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was seized in a raid in Sinaloa that set off gunfights and roadblocks across the state.
body: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as Chapo Isidro, was captured on Friday in Sinaloa in a special forces raid coordinated with US intelligence. He was on the FBI's list of ten most wanted fugitives.

Mexico's defence ministry said on Sunday that eight suspected members of a gang linked to him had been arrested, including a minor. It said on Saturday that seven suspected attackers and four soldiers had been killed.
The US ambassador, Ronald Johnson, said intelligence sharing helped make the operation possible. Meza Flores, 44, faces charges in both Mexico and the United States.

stories.head: Kim Jong-un pledges wider foreign ties after declining Trump meeting
stories.say: Kim Jong-un says North Korea will expand its foreign relations while protecting its sovereignty, days after Donald Trump left Asia without the meeting he had sought.
stories.stand: North Korea's leader personally received new ambassadors, including Russia's, in a rare break from protocol.
body: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un said his country would expand foreign relations under the ideals of independence, peace and friendship, state media reported on Monday.
He spoke while receiving the credentials of new ambassadors, including Russia's, a task usually done by a senior official. Kim said North Korea pursued neither supremacy nor expansion.
The remarks came days after President Donald Trump left Asia without meeting Kim, despite trying to arrange talks during his trip to China.

stories.head: Eisenkot calls settler arson attacks in West Bank 'Jewish terrorism'
stories.say: Settlers set fire to cars and homes in several Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank on Sunday. Israel's opposition leader, Gadi Eisenkot, called it Jewish terrorism.
stories.stand: Twelve vehicles were reportedly burned in at least five villages, and police said no arrests had been made.
body: Settlers set fire to vehicles and homes in several Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank early on Sunday. Twelve vehicles were reportedly set alight in at least five villages, including seven cars in Kafr Malik.
Gadi Eisenkot, the opposition leader charged with forming Israel's next government, called the attacks Jewish terrorism and called for arrests. He blamed Benjamin Netanyahu's government.
The Israeli military condemned the violence. Police said they were investigating, and no arrests had been reported. The UN says there have been six settler attacks a day on average in 2026.

stories.head: National strike against austerity grounds flights across Belgium
stories.say: A national strike against government spending cuts grounded flights across Belgium on Monday. Brussels Airport cancelled every flight between seven in the morning and nine at night.
stories.stand: Unions walked out over plans to save €10bn, as Prime Minister Bart De Wever tries to agree next year's budget.
body: Trade unions held a national strike in Belgium on Monday against the federal government's austerity plans. Air traffic controller Skeyes said it could not provide regular services, grounding planes across the country.
Brussels Airport cancelled all flights from 7am to 9pm. Trains, buses and schools were also disrupted.

The government wants to save €10bn in the coming years. Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered his resignation, but King Philippe declined it. De Wever has set a deadline of 31 December for a budget deal.

stories.head: Iran flogs singer who performed without hijab, her lawyer says
stories.say: Iran has flogged the singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her team over an online concert she gave without a hijab, according to her lawyer.
stories.stand: Parastoo Ahmadi's 2024 concert near Qom was streamed on YouTube with no audience.
body: Iran flogged pop singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her concert team on Monday, her lawyer, Mostafa Nili, said.

A criminal court in Qom province sentenced nine members of the team to 74 lashes each, plus two-year bans on leaving the country and on artistic work. The charge was offending public decency by producing vulgar content online.

Ahmadi performed without a hijab at a historic caravanserai near Qom in December 2024. The concert had no audience and was broadcast on YouTube. Amnesty International had called for the sentences to be quashed.

stories.head: Penny Wong warns US-China rivalry is raising risk of conflict
stories.say: Australia's foreign minister, Penny Wong, is warning that rivalry between the United States and China is making the world less stable and raising the risk of conflict.
stories.stand: Australia's foreign minister previewed a major address to the Senate due on Tuesday.
body: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong will warn in a Senate address on Tuesday that rivalry between the US and China is making the world less stable, ABC News reported.

She will say both powers are increasingly willing to use power without regard for the rules that have helped prevent major conflict. She will say China is carrying out the largest military build-up of any country since the Second World War.
Wong will urge middle powers not to abandon multilateralism and call for reform, including of the UN Security Council.

stories.head: Co-op Live evacuated after unknown substance released at concert
stories.say: More than twelve thousand people were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live arena on Sunday night after an unknown substance was released at a Don Toliver concert.
stories.stand: Police declared a major incident and are investigating what the substance was and how it was released.
body: Greater Manchester Police declared a major incident shortly after 10pm on Sunday when a substance was released in the crowd at a Don Toliver concert at Co-op Live. More than 12,000 people were evacuated, CBS News reported.
North West Ambulance Service said more than 50 people were assessed, some with eye and breathing symptoms. One person was taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary.

Police first believed the substance was tear gas, but it has not been confirmed. Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker said officers would now work to understand what it was and how the incident happened.

stories.head: Snow and frost forecast as winter makes an early arrival
stories.say: Parts of the UK are bracing for an early taste of winter, with frost, freezing fog and snow on Scottish high ground forecast for Tuesday, and a cold health alert across northern England.
stories.stand: A yellow cold health alert covers northern England, and heavy rain returns to the South West on Tuesday.
body: The Met Office says winter will make an early arrival for some this week, with colder air from Scandinavia meeting milder Atlantic weather. Rural Scotland could fall to minus 9C, with freezing fog possible in the Midlands.
Rain returns to South West England and South Wales on Tuesday, with snow likely on higher ground in Scotland. Wednesday and Thursday are expected to be drier but colder.

The UK Health Security Agency has a yellow cold health alert for the North West, North East and Yorkshire and the Humber. The UK's coldest night since 9 January was on Friday, at minus 10.6C in Tulloch Bridge.

stories.head: Flooding closes roads across south Cornwall
stories.say: Flooding left roads impassable across south Cornwall on Sunday, with Falmouth among the worst-hit places. The Environment Agency warns river levels will stay high into this week.
stories.stand: Falmouth was among the worst-hit towns, and more heavy rain is forecast for Monday and Tuesday.
body: Flooding made roads impassable across south Cornwall on Sunday while a yellow Met Office rain warning was in force. In Falmouth, water was reported on Arwenack Street, Bank Place and Swanpool Street.
The B3304 Porthleven Road near Helston was blocked in both directions. The Environment Agency said flooding was possible around The Lizard, Penryn, Falmouth and Truro.
It said river levels would stay high into this week, with more heavy rain forecast for Monday and Tuesday. It urged people not to walk, cycle or drive through floodwater.

stories.head: Strikes begin at Trident nuclear weapons depot in Coulport
stories.say: Workers at the Royal Naval Armaments Depot in Coulport, which serves the Trident nuclear system, are striking over pay. The Unite union warns it could affect defence capabilities.
stories.stand: About 70 Unite members at the Argyll and Bute site are walking out in turn this week after rejecting pay offers.
body: About 70 Unite members at the Royal Naval Armaments Depot in Coulport, Argyll and Bute, are striking over pay. They work for the ABL Alliance, which holds a Ministry of Defence contract to service the Trident nuclear weapons system.
AWE workers strike on 23 November, Lockheed Martin members on 24 November and Babcock Marine members on 26 November. An overtime ban has been in place since 9 November.
Unite said the strikes would hit the UK's nuclear and defence response capabilities. The MoD said it was disappointed no agreement had been reached and urged both sides to keep talking.

stories.head: Man jailed for life for drowning woman in Thames at Henley club
stories.say: A kitchen porter has been jailed for life, with a minimum of twenty-two and a half years, for murdering a woman in the River Thames at a members' club in Henley.
stories.stand: Nelio Gouveia admitted murder at Oxford Crown Court; the attack happened in March at Phyllis Court.
body: Nelio Gouveia, 45, has been jailed for life at Oxford Crown Court, with a minimum term of 22 years and six months, for murder. He had admitted the killing last month.
He worked at Phyllis Court, a private members' club in Henley-on-Thames. Police found the 44-year-old victim's body in the River Thames on 6 March.
The prosecution said he struck her with a metal bar and held her under water. Mr Justice Jay said the murder was fuelled by drugs, alcohol and his appetite for violent pornography.

stories.head: Second group of Gaza children arrives in UK for NHS treatment
stories.say: A second group of critically ill and injured children from Gaza has arrived in the UK with their families for specialist NHS treatment, the government says.
stories.stand: The evacuation was led by a cross-government taskforce with the World Health Organization.
body: A group of critically ill and injured children from Gaza has arrived in the UK with close family members for specialist NHS treatment, the Department of Health said on 23 November.
The evacuation was led by a cross-government taskforce with the World Health Organization, supported by British Embassy staff in Amman. Last year's evacuations brought 50 children to NHS hospitals.
The government will not disclose the children's identities or where they are being treated. It said more evacuations are expected before the end of 2026.

stories.head: UK pledges £18m for security in British Overseas Territories
stories.say: The government is putting eighteen million pounds into tackling organised crime and violence in the British Overseas Territories, as their leaders meet in London.
stories.stand: The funding was announced as leaders gathered in London for the four-day Joint Ministerial Council.
body: The government announced £18m on 23 November to tackle organised crime, violence and emerging security threats in the British Overseas Territories.

The money covers policing, criminal justice and prisons, maritime security, cyber and safeguarding. It was announced as the annual Joint Ministerial Council opened in London, running until 26 November.
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called the territories an essential part of the British family of nations.

stories.stand: The Nottingham project also promises shops, offices and up to 2,000 jobs.
body: Homes England has launched the search for a lead development partner for Broad Marsh in Nottingham. The scheme plans about 1,000 homes and up to 2,000 jobs.

Bidders must respond by 8 January 2027, and a partner is expected to be appointed in mid-2027.

stories.head: Burnham takes EU deal to MPs as retailers doubt prices will fall
stories.say: Andy Burnham is promoting his new EU deal, saying it will take pressure off food prices. Retailers welcome it, but the British Retail Consortium doesn't expect shelf prices to fall.
stories.stand: The Prime Minister visited a Kent supermarket before a Commons statement on the deals struck at last week's Brussels summit.
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited a Morrisons in Kent on Monday to promote the deals agreed at Friday's Brussels summit, before addressing MPs. He says the food deal is taking pressure off the cost of food and could raise GDP by 0.4%.
The agreement ends most post-Brexit checks on food and agricultural products from 1 March 2028. Further deals cover emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.

The British Retail Consortium called it a big win for retailers but did not expect shelf prices to fall. Ministers declined to say how much prices would drop. Tory deputy leader Alex Burghart said his party would repeal the deal.

stories.head: May and Sunak warn Burnham against reopening Brexit debate
stories.say: Theresa May and Rishi Sunak have both warned Andy Burnham against reopening the Brexit debate. May said she was aghast, while Sunak called it divisive and all-consuming.
stories.stand: Two former Conservative prime ministers joined Boris Johnson and David Cameron in criticising the Prime Minister's plans on EU ties.
body: Former Prime Minister Theresa May told the BBC on Sunday that Andy Burnham should accept Brexit and move on. She said she was aghast at his push to reopen the debate.
Rishi Sunak told Sky News that reopening the debate would be divisive and an all-consuming distraction. He said he did not expect the UK to rejoin the EU within five years.
Boris Johnson and David Cameron had earlier issued similar warnings. Labour's Tony Blair said Britain should rejoin only if the EU reforms.

stories.stand: Unnamed party insiders told ITV Border the SNP would use budget votes to press demands later.

Senior figures believe they could use budget votes to press demands including a second independence referendum. Burnham has repeatedly said that question is off the table.

stories.head: Louise Haigh tells CBI energy and water reforms will cut costs
stories.say: Louise Haigh told the CBI conference that ten thousand manufacturers will be able to take up to forty pounds per megawatt hour off their electricity bills from April.
stories.stand: The First Secretary of State made 'the business case for public control' at the CBI's annual conference.
body: First Secretary of State Louise Haigh gave the keynote speech at the CBI annual conference on 23 November, titled the business case for public control.
She said a British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme will let 10,000 manufacturers take up to £40 per MWh off bills from April. She said a Water Bill will create a single independent regulator.
Haigh said reform of arm's length bodies has begun with the Environment Agency, Natural England, Ofwat and the Drinking Water Inspectorate.

stories.say: Jon Ossoff's eighteen-point re-election win in Georgia has sparked talk of a 2028 presidential run, though he has said he has zero interest in running.
stories.stand: The Georgia senator beat Republican Mike Collins by about 18 points and now leads one early poll.
body: Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff, 39, won re-election in Georgia by about 18 points over Republican Mike Collins, CBS News reported. He won in 2020 by just over one point.
A post-election Emerson College poll gave him 17% in a hypothetical 2028 Democratic primary, narrowly ahead of Kamala Harris and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
Ossoff said in an October debate that he had zero interest in running for president in 2028. CBS exit polling found he won 40% of white voters, against 28% for Harris in 2024.

stories.head: US appeals court strikes down pregnant workers law
stories.say: A US appeals court has struck down the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act by nine votes to eight, ruling that Congress passed it unconstitutionally using proxy votes.
stories.stand: The 5th Circuit ruled 9-8 that proxy voting during Covid did not meet the Constitution's quorum rule.
body: The 5th Circuit Court of Appeals has struck down the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act, which requires workplaces to accommodate pregnancy and childbirth. The full court ruled 9-8 on Friday.
It held that Congress violated the Constitution in 2022 because most House members were not physically present. Pandemic rules allowed proxy votes, which the court said do not count towards a quorum.
Advocates say the ruling invalidates the law in Texas, Louisiana and Mississippi. A Better Balance said it would likely be appealed to the Supreme Court.

stories.say: California voters have rejected a one-off five per cent tax on billionaires' wealth, after opponents outspent supporters ten to one.
stories.stand: Proposition 40 failed with 52% voting no, while a measure banning future wealth taxes narrowly passed.
body: California voters rejected Proposition 40, a one-off 5% tax on the wealth of residents worth more than $1bn, with 52% voting no. Most of the money would have gone to healthcare.
Voters narrowly approved Proposition 42, which bans future state taxes on financial assets and business interests. Only a future ballot measure can override it.
A committee against the tax raised more than $333m, and opponents outspent supporters 10 to 1, AP reported.

stories.say: The leaders of Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Poland have raised concerns about the EU's next long-term budget, with Hungary's Péter Magyar opposing Ukraine funding in it.
stories.stand: The Visegrád Four and Austria met in Bratislava but adopted no joint position.
body: Prime ministers of the Visegrád Four met in Bratislava on Monday with Austria's chancellor and raised concerns about the EU's next seven-year budget proposal.

Hungary's Péter Magyar said the proposal was not an acceptable starting point and that support for Ukraine should not be in the EU budget. The Czech Republic's Andrej Babiš called the Parliament's three sites unnecessary and costly.
Slovakia's Robert Fico, the host, said the leaders did not adopt a joint position. Poland's Donald Tusk stressed continued support for Kyiv but said joint borrowing was not a good way to fund it.

stories.say: Spain votes on Sunday, with polls putting Alberto Núñez Feijóo's Popular Party ahead of Pedro Sánchez's Socialists but short of a majority.
stories.stand: Polls suggest the Popular Party would need far-right Vox to reach a majority on 29 November.
body: Spain holds a general election on 29 November. Opinion polls put the conservative Popular Party, led by Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ahead of Pedro Sánchez's Socialists but short of a majority.
Projections cited by Al Jazeera give the PP 127 seats and the PSOE 119, with 176 needed for a majority. The far-right Vox party is polling third.
Feijóo, 65, led Galicia's regional government from 2009 to 2022. He prefers to govern alone with Vox's support but has not ruled out a formal coalition.

stories.say: Nvidia has brought back Jensen Huang as chief executive, eleven days after he resigned. The shares jumped by about a third on Monday.
stories.stand: The board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang, who quit on 12 November after reports of extramarital affairs.
body: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and chief executive with immediate effect on Monday. He resigned on 12 November after reports of extramarital affairs.
Reuters reported that one affair involved a woman US authorities suspect of spying for China, which Beijing denies. Interim chief executive Colette Kress will remain finance chief.
Nvidia shares rose more than 30% on Monday. President Donald Trump called the decision correct and proper. Senator Elizabeth Warren called it reckless.

stories.say: Wall Street bounced back on Monday, with the Nasdaq up about seven per cent, after last week's tech rout. Earlier, Seoul's Kospi had closed down more than three per cent.
stories.stand: Huang's return to Nvidia lifted US indices, after a sell-off that had pushed the S&P 500 into a correction.
body: US stocks rallied on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang. About two hours into trading, the Nasdaq was up 7%, the S&P 500 5% and the Dow Jones 2.6%, Euronews reported.

stories.stand: The plant in Estarreja will be LEGO's fourth in Europe and its most automated, the company says.
body: LEGO announced on Monday that it will invest around €1bn over several years in a new factory in Estarreja, Portugal. It will employ more than 1,000 people once fully operational.

stories.stand: The domestic edition of the summit came as Emmanuel Macron pledged €350m for aeronautics research.
body: French companies presented 273 industrial projects worth €42.5bn at the Choose France summit in Paris on Monday, of which €14.9bn is new investment.
Two programmes make up over 40% of the total: €9.5bn from airports group ADP and €8bn from grid operator RTE.

stories.say: More than twenty-three thousand workers at nineteen sites in northern Germany were called out on a twenty-four hour strike, hitting Mercedes-Benz and BMW.
stories.stand: IG Metall is seeking a 5% pay rise; employers have offered a one-off payment and a later 1.3% rise.
body: IG Metall called more than 23,000 workers at 19 sites in northern Germany out on a 24-hour strike from Sunday evening. Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Siemens Gamesa were hit.

stories.stand: Imports of the materials rose 25% in a year, and the EU's deficit with China has hit €1bn a day.
body: The European Commission launched a trade defence investigation on Monday into a surge of cheap composite resin and glass fibre imports, mainly from China. Imports have risen 25% in the past year.
The probe is expected to last nine to 11 months and could lead to quotas or tariffs. Any safeguard measures would apply to imports from all trading partners.
The materials are used in renewable energy, transport, aerospace and defence. Separately, an EU deal letting in 350,000 Chinese hybrid cars a year takes effect on 1 December.

body: South Korea and China have largely completed talks to expand their free trade agreement to cover entertainment, tourism and financial services.

Protests since October have closed around 500 of more than 4,000 clothing factories. The industry employs around four million people.

stories.stand: The supplier, serving about 2.4 million customers, faced a £30.5m Ofwat settlement and heatwave costs.
body: South East Water made a pre-tax loss of £22.9m in the six months to 30 September, against an £18.2m profit a year earlier.

The company, which serves about 2.4 million customers, raised £50m in emergency shareholder funding in October. It says it is seeing early signs of improvement.

stories.stand: The joint European and Japanese probe will split into two orbiters in December and start science work in April 2027.
body: The BepiColombo probe has entered orbit around Mercury after an eight-year journey, the European Space Agency said early on Sunday. ESA said the spacecraft was in contact with the ground.

stories.stand: University of Sydney researchers say stars are forming along a shock front at the edge of the galaxy's central bar.
body: Astronomers led by the University of Sydney say part of the Milky Way's Norma arm may be star formation along the leading edge of the galaxy's central bar, rather than a spiral arm.
They compared large galaxy simulations with observations of massive star-forming regions. Masers once linked to the Norma arm line up with a shock front predicted by the simulations.
The study in Nature Astronomy says the bar reaches about 14,000 light-years from the galactic centre. Shock fronts in other barred galaxies usually suppress star formation.

body: University of Miami researchers have identified a previously unknown group of viruses with smaller, simpler genomes than related shell-forming viruses.

stories.stand: Dr Miles Russell of Bournemouth University points to Verica's name and coin imagery.
body: Dr Miles Russell of Bournemouth University argues that Verica, ruler of the Atrebates in what is now Hampshire and West Sussex, was a woman, not a man as long assumed.

body: Researchers at the University of California, Davis, have sequenced the genome of the trapdoor spider Aptostichus stephencolberti. It is about 4.6 billion base pairs, roughly 50% larger than the human genome.
The spider has 52 chromosomes, against 46 in humans, and about 77% of its genome is repetitive DNA. It is the first sequenced genome from its family.
The species lives in coastal dunes from the San Francisco Bay area to Monterey, leaving it vulnerable to sea-level rise.

stories.stand: University of Basel researchers found two groups of neurons that track how long mice have been awake.
body: Researchers at the University of Basel identified two groups of brainstem neurons that became more active the longer mice stayed awake.

stories.stand: Université de Montréal astronomers say the red dwarf's stable orbit is hard to explain.
body: Astronomers led by Étienne Artigau of the Université de Montréal have found a hidden white dwarf in a system about 28 light-years from Earth, Space.com reported. The system, named Welopō'ai, has a red dwarf and two white dwarfs.

stories.say: A bill in Kenya's parliament would make metered, pay-for-what-you-use internet billing compulsory. The communications regulator and a major telecoms firm have raised concerns.
stories.stand: The communications regulator and Telkom Kenya warn of affordability, privacy and investment effects.
body: A Kenyan bill would make consumption-based internet billing mandatory, with each customer given a unique meter number. A parliamentary committee is considering it.
The Communications Authority of Kenya cautioned against compulsory metered billing, citing affordability and digital inclusion. It proposed usage alerts and spending caps instead.
Telkom Kenya said mobile internet, about 96% of data subscriptions, is already billed by volume, so the change would mainly hit fixed broadband. It warned of privacy risks and higher costs.

stories.stand: The claim, from the company's press release, has not been independently confirmed.
body: A German-Ukrainian joint venture said on Monday that its SPYS interceptor drone shot down a Russian jet-powered Geran-5 drone during combat testing in Ukraine.
The venture was set up by German defence firm Quantum Systems and Ukraine's WIY Drones. WIY says SPYS has a top speed of around 450kph.
Ukraine's military intelligence says the jet-powered Geran-5 can be classed as a compact cruise missile. The shootdown claim has not been independently confirmed.

stories.stand: Nikol Pashinyan said data centre growth means Armenia now needs to import electricity.
body: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan announced plans to connect Armenia's power grid with those of Azerbaijan and Turkey, speaking at the DigiTec 2026 conference in Yerevan.

stories.say: South Korea's education minister, Choi Kyo-jin, has resigned after criticism of last-minute measures to stop AI-assisted cheating in the national university entrance exam.
stories.stand: Choi Kyo-jin admitted the government had not prepared adequately for the university entrance exam.
body: South Korea's Education Minister, Choi Kyo-jin, resigned after criticism of last-minute measures to stop AI-assisted cheating on the national university entrance exam. President Lee Jae-myung accepted the resignation on Sunday.
About 8,400 extra staff were deployed and three emergency phone alerts were sent to find hidden devices. There were 111 suspected cases involving electronic devices.
The ministry said it would file criminal complaints against five candidates caught using smart devices.

stories.say: Ireland's recycling compliance body says only three in ten small electrical items are recycled, and warns that batteries thrown in bins can cause fires.
stories.stand: WEEE Ireland warns that batteries thrown in household bins can start fires in waste trucks.
body: Just three in 10 small electrical items are recycled, according to figures from WEEE Ireland. For electronic toys, the rate is 10%.
Of more than 33 million small electrical items sold in Ireland last year, 40% were bought during the festive period.
Elizabeth O'Reilly of WEEE Ireland said used batteries should never go into household bins, because they can be crushed and cause fires in bin trucks.

stories.say: Paolo Bulgari, the jeweller who chaired the family firm as it grew into a global luxury brand, has died in Rome at the age of eighty-nine.
stories.stand: The grandson of the firm's founder chaired it as it grew into watches, perfume and leather goods.
body: Paolo Bulgari, the Italian jeweller and grandson of the company's founder, has died in Rome aged 89, his family announced on Saturday.
He became chairman in 1984 and, with his brother and nephew, expanded the firm into watches, perfumes and leather goods. In 2011 the family sold its controlling stake to LVMH for about €3.7bn.
His family called him the greatest jeweller of our time. His funeral is on Monday at the Basilica of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme.

stories.head: Hidden tunnels uncovered beneath Istanbul's Hagia Sophia
stories.say: Excavation beneath Istanbul's Hagia Sophia has cleared four hundred and twenty metres of tunnels and uncovered ancient water networks, some possibly older than the basilica.
stories.stand: Some remains may predate the 6th-century basilica, but their dating has not been confirmed.
body: Cleaning and excavation at Hagia Sophia in Istanbul have uncovered underground galleries, ancient water networks and architectural remains. So far 420 metres of tunnels have been cleaned.
Almost 3,000 tonnes of backfill have been removed. Six underground spaces and nine tunnels have been identified, the longest 180 metres.
Some remains may predate the current 6th-century basilica, but scientists have not confirmed their dating. Culture Minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy toured the site.

stories.stand: The Spaniard saved three set points in the tie-break to beat the world number one in Turin.

Alcaraz joins Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic as the only men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.

stories.stand: Eighth place at the Portuguese Grand Prix was enough for the Ducati rider's second title in a row.

stories.say: The Court of Arbitration for Sport announces on Tuesday whether Senegal can keep the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, which was handed to Morocco after Senegal's walk-off.
stories.stand: African football's governing body awarded the title to Morocco after Senegal walked off in the final.
body: The Court of Arbitration for Sport will announce on Tuesday its decision on Senegal's appeal against being stripped of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title.
